pages.title: Lamps
pages.content: Six pieces stand on the floor this month: floor, table and pendant lamps, each chosen for one room. The floor is re-set on the first Wednesday of every month, and any piece can be borrowed for a 7-day home trial.

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content: Which room is the lamp for? Dining rooms, reading corners, living rooms, halls and stairs, and kitchen tables each need a different height, glare and colour temperature.

pages.title: Fitting & Specification
pages.content: A 90-minute home consultation costs €120. We deliver a written light plan with lamp positions, 2700K bulbs and dimmers, and you can test up to three pieces for 7 days against a refundable €50 deposit.

pages.title: Projects
pages.content: Four rooms, lit after dark: a stone bay in Kralingen, Café Noor with 28 seats, a reading corner under the stairs and a kitchen table for six.

posts.title: Rewiring a 1960s brass lamp
posts.excerpt: A look inside our workshop bench as Sam Okoro restores original brass switchgear, replaces perished braided cord, and fits modern ceramic E27 sockets.
posts.content:
A lamp from the 1960s usually arrives with brittle cloth cord and a socket that no longer holds a bulb straight. Sam Okoro strips it to the brass, tests every part and keeps what can be kept.

The new cord is braided cotton, the socket is ceramic E27, and the lamp leaves the bench with a safety test. Rewiring and repair starts from €65.

posts.title: How a linen shade is made
posts.excerpt: Shade maker Lucía Ferraz demonstrates the careful process of patterning, tensioning, and hand-stretching unbleached linen over solid wire drum frames.
posts.content:
Lucía Ferraz starts with a paper pattern cut to the frame, then stretches unbleached linen over a wire drum, pinning it while it is still slack.

The seam is glued, the edges are bound by hand, and the shade is tested on a 2700K bulb before it joins the floor.
